Sorry for the delay in replying. I only get notified about homekit_controller tickets when a label is applied (thanks @spacegaier for tagging it for me). (Normally a bot does this if it sees the URL for the homekit documentation in the original ticket).

I'm guessing if you look in your config dir in `.storage/homekit_controller-entity-map.json` you'll both find one of the characteristics in that file with values that match your anomalous "spikes". My theory is it's captured a stray temperature reading at the point in time where you paired your devices, and is loading that one at startup. If you are able to confirm thats the case it will be a big help.

If that is the case then a workaround for now is to edit the JSON to make sure that the value is inside the range that won't trigger your alarm.

The "proper" fix will probably be to change the homekit client to start in an `unavailable` state so it can't report old values.  It might be a while before I have time to take that on, though.
Yes, that looks exactly what's happening. In my example above, the two stored characteristic values are 0 (32F) and 18.4 (65.1F).

It's a _very_ naive change, but initting the devices as unavailable avoids the jump in my local testing: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/commit/08e228ec2d3533136c0121235962827f1f34d21a#

The entities start up with an `unavailable` state, but that's likely the correct state until we can get a fresh value.

It breaks one test which I haven't had time to dig into yet. @Jc2k is this too simple of a fix or is this along the lines of what you were considering?

Ah, interesting. I was so wrapped up in changing aiohomekit's data model (so that it can handle partial unavailability on a bridge with e.g. multiple bulbs) that I didn't even consider a "quick win" fix like that for this case. I'd take a PR for that change if you can figure out the test.
I'm unfortunately still seeing this in 2021.6.0.

The behavior is different where the entities are set to `unavailable` on startup, but they seem to be marked as available too early before a fresh value is received:
```
2021-06-02 @ 16:16:36.903640 -- sensor.front_room_temperature_homekit | 74.1
2021-06-02 @ 16:36:51.869276 -- sensor.front_room_temperature_homekit | 74.3

```

@jjlawren If you turn on debug logs for `homeassistant.components.homekit_controller` do you see something like:

> HomeKit connection not polling any characteristics: xxxxxxxxxxxx

If you do, can you try this change. In `homeassistant/components/homekit_controller/connection.py` in the `HKDevice.async_update` function you should see:

```python
        if not self.pollable_characteristics:
            self.async_set_available_state(self.pairing.connection.is_connected)
            _LOGGER.debug(
                "HomeKit connection not polling any characteristics: %s", self.unique_id
            )
            return
```

Remove the call to `set_available_state`. `self.pollable_characteristics` will be empty at startup until all the entities had registered the characteristics they want to poll and the ones they want to subscribe to. So in my mind the entity isn't really available at that point anyway.

The other possible cause is *something* other than a poll is calling `process_new_events` during startup. Every call to `process_new_events` switches the device back to available. An single event could switch all entities on a bridge back to the available state. The only fixes I can see there are:

* Modify the aiohomekit model not to restore the underlying state. This is way harder than it sounds because none of the homeassistant code has a concept of "not loaded yet". 
* Modify the underlying aiohomekit model to start in an unavailable state. This would probably overlap with https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/51077? This is slightly annoying because an accessory will always be in a partially loaded state (we never poll *every* characteristic). The helpers in aiohomekit thus wouldn't work (`accessory.available` checks the state of every char...)
* Only call `self.async_set_available_state(True)` after a poll. This feels like papering over the problem, but is probably simplest.
* Add some kind of ready state. Entity stays `unavailable` until something marks it `ready` (probably the poll).

@Jc2k `HomeKit connection not polling any characteristics` is not in the logs. However, do these logs imply they're marked as available before polling?:

Yep. Studying the code, one of those is that aiohomekit now sends an empty event when the connection is restored after an outage (so home assistant notices connection is back). Not sure about the other.

This means it's going to need a more involved fix from my list I think. You could test my theory by getting rid of `self.async_set_available_state(True)` in `process_new_events`, then add one to `async_update` (at the end, after it calls process_events). I don't think this is the fix we should apply, but it helps confirm whats going on.
Got around to testing your suggested change, and it does avoid the "bad" value jump on startup. It will instead be `unavailable` for ~2-5 seconds before a current & "good" value is used.
@Jc2k do you still think the above change is the wrong approach? It seems to be effective in my environment. I can make a PR if you've changed your view.

I want to get https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/51077 in first and then see where we are at. Work on it has already started (see https://github.com/Jc2k/aiohomekit/pull/36) and @bdraco has ordered some bridge based devices to test it out, so i hope that won't delay things too much.

I think the quick and dirty approach i suggested here is a bit of a hack that is paving over a design issue, and if you do that enough times you end up with brittle hard to test code thats annoying to refactor. I think #51077 unlocks less hacky approaches.

Whenever I restart HA, temperature goes to 212F and humidity goes to 100% for about 20 seconds, haha.

I think we can fix this once https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/73806 is merged since the deadlock that prevented awaiting the platform setup should be gone, but it might also need some refactoring
I think to fully fix this we need to wait for the connection at startup and raise `ConfigEntryNotReady` when we cannot connect as well as await the platform setups

```diff
diff --git a/homeassistant/components/homekit_controller/connection.py b/homeassistant/components/homekit_controller/connection.py
index 8b5dd55a57d..b9dc906ca6b 100644
--- a/homeassistant/components/homekit_controller/connection.py
+++ b/homeassistant/components/homekit_controller/connection.py
@@ -199,7 +199,7 @@ class HKDevice:
             self.hass, self.async_update, DEFAULT_SCAN_INTERVAL
         )
 
-        self.hass.async_create_task(self.async_process_entity_map())
+        await self.async_process_entity_map()
 
         return True
 
```

But we need to make sure that connection failure timeout doesn't block startup and if a connection loop is started its not in a tracked task

This code predates the entity registry being able to restore unavailable entities. It used to effectively try and simulate that using the cached entity maps.

It does have an edge case already where if there is no cached entity map and it can't fetch one it does a ConfigNotReady iirc.

We could just always take that route now, which might simplify things.

review_comments: While right now its always going to be there since we only support IP, but since we are adding BLE/thread, longer term, it might be better to have pairing return a better error about why it cannot connect.
